writeup.headline: Fastly rates Hold: accelerating growth and net cash offset by losses, heavy dilution and a demanding valuation.
writeup.thesis: Fastly scores 52, a Hold, because strong growth and a solid balance sheet are balanced by weak profitability and a very low valuation score. Growth scores 75 on latest-quarter revenue growth of 23.3% year on year and TTM revenue growth of 20.4%, with growth sped up by 3.5 pp from the previous quarter, and the balance sheet scores 92 thanks to net cash. Quality scores only 30: the operating margin is -12.0%, stock-based compensation runs at 19.7% of revenue and the diluted share count is up 8.1% year on year, though the FCF margin is a positive 7.4%. Valuation scores 9, with P/S of 6.3x and P/FCF of 85.0x high in absolute terms, FCF yield 3.8 pp below the 10-year Treasury yield, and P/S more expensive than at 54 of the last 61 month-ends. The trend score of 75 reflects shares up 206.2% from 12 months ago to 1 month ago, though they trail SPY and QQQ over the last 126 trading days, and news is mildly positive at 56.
key_risks: Q3 results on 2026-11-04 could disappoint after the raised full-year outlook and a large share-price run.
Continued operating losses and stock-based compensation of 19.7% of revenue keep diluting holders.
Valuation is high in absolute terms, leaving little cushion if growth slows.
Insider selling by the CEO and CTO through October, with no purchases.
The pending Kula v. Fastly securities class action and reliance on large customers.
what_would_change: An upgrade to Buy needs 13 more points, most plausibly from better quality (narrower operating losses, lower dilution) or a lower valuation multiple.
A drop of 8 points would mean Sell, for example if growth decelerates in the Q3 report or the share-price trend breaks down.
A guidance cut or negative analyst and insider news would pull the news score lower.
